note: Choose a trail of maximum edge-length, which exists because the graph is finite and has an edge. If its endpoints differ, arrivals/departures at the terminal endpoint pair except for the final arrival, so the trail uses an odd number of incident edges there. Even total degree leaves an unused incident edge, contradicting maximality. Thus the trail is closed. If an edge is omitted, connectedness and a shortest path from an endpoint of that edge to the trail yield an unused edge incident to a trail vertex. Rotate the closed trail to that vertex and append the unused edge, again contradicting maximality. Therefore the longest trail is a closed traversal of every edge exactly once.
